title: Ferdinand I to Johann Malvezzi, Augsburg, 23 January 1548 (DECODE R366)

steps.what: Fetched the eight R366 images and the record metadata from DECODE with a saved cookie.

Web searches for a published decipherment of the letter and for the Ferdinand-Malvezzi ciphers. No decipherment found; identified Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 as the edition that probably prints the letter, not freely available online.
Searched the DECODE record list around R366 and found the key records R367 (same shelfmark) and R386, with transcriptions DOC_R367 and DOC_R386.
Calibrated the sign values on p. 1 against the key images (sermone, tecum, quod, propter, tractatum, nobiscum, constituendae, autor).
Read the cipher runs page by page from zoomed crops, two subagents in parallel on pp. 1/4/7 and pp. 5/6. p. 4 read almost in full, pp. 5-6 read, pp. 1 and 7 read in part.

Looked for the letter in Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 via web search, the H-Net review and footnotes in Tracy, 'The Logic of Kleinkrieg' (AHY 2021) and Gürkan/Levantine Heritage papers. The edition is not online (no Google Books/HathiTrust full view found). Established only its neighbours: instructions for Malvezzi 24 Jan 1548 (reportedly no. 62), Ferdinand to Justus de Argento 13 Feb 1548 = no. 68, pp. 213-15. The 23 Jan letter's own number and text could not be seen, so the reading is neither confirmed nor corrected.

outcome.method_basis: The key is DECODE R367, a reconstruction filed at the same shelfmark (Military History Archive 1548/3), with a second copy R386; its sign values were calibrated on p. 1 and the cipher runs read from zoomed crops of R366.
outcome.notes: The substance is recovered: the French are working to break the Habsburg-Ottoman peace because they dare not attack Charles V directly; the Sultan and Ruestem Pasha are not to doubt Habsburg sincerity; and Malvezzi is granted 1,500 ducats a year, to be brought by a secretary. Short stretches on pp. 1 and 7 are unread. fraction_read 0.9 is an estimate: about 22 of 150 reading lines in read_A.md/read_B.md still carry [?] or [...] marks, concentrated on pp. 1, 6 foot and 7.

gaps.detail: read_A.md p1 l3-l4 still carry [?] and [...] groups; glyphs transcribed, no second pass with the R367 key recorded

gaps.item: p. 6 foot, last lines (what to say if Ruestem Pasha asks about the border)
gaps.detail: NOTES: "partly unread"; no further attempt recorded

gaps.item: p. 7 ciphered passage on the captives, partly unread
gaps.detail: NOTES: "partly read"; read_A.md p7 lines still carry [?] groups

outcome.fraction_read_source: read_A.md + read_B.md (pp. 1, 4-7): per reading line, units = max(cipher word groups excluding declared nulls, plaintext words); words carrying [?], [..], [...] or ? counted unread: 442/530 = 0.83 (plain word count 443/521 = 0.85). Script measure_B_malvezzi.py (session scratchpad).

prior.where: No decipherment on DECODE or the web. Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 (Munich 1995) prints the Ferdinand-Malvezzi correspondence of early 1548 (Ferdinand's instructions for Malvezzi, 24 Jan 1548, reportedly no. 62; Ferdinand to Justus de Argento, Augsburg 13 Feb 1548, no. 68, pp. 213-15, per Tracy 2021), so this 23 Jan 1548 letter is probably printed there around nos. 62-67 (c. pp. 190-212); number unconfirmed, edition not online, not consulted (checked 2026-09-21).

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, and set the target with /goal. No target-specific intervention.
